entries.name: Zero items collected, exit 0
entries.definition: The runner executed successfully and collected nothing, which is reported as success.
detection_signal: Run your suite with an explicitly empty selection (-k "zzz_no_match", --filter that matches nothing, an empty target list).
If it exits 0, you have this bug.
Separately, verify the mapping itself: assert every declared target exists before running anything.
entries.gate_mapping: Make an empty collection a failure, and validate the mapping before use.

required_evidence.control: Empty the target list / rename one target
required_evidence.expected: exits non-zero with 0 targets collected or N declared targets missing

required_evidence.control: Point the runner at a non-existent directory
required_evidence.expected: exits non-zero, not collected 0 items + exit 0

entries.name: Early return as an implicit skip
entries.definition: A guard exits the test body instead of reporting a skip — so the test appears to have passed.
detection_signal: Grep your suite for bare return statements inside test functions, and for if not <condition> guards with no else.
Compare the reported test count against the number of test functions. Equal counts with unexpected green is the signature.
Run the suite in both environments (with and without the precondition met) and diff the skip counts.
entries.gate_mapping: Convert the silent exit into an explicit skip, or into an outright failure if the precondition is required.

required_evidence.expected: test reports skipped (or failed if required) — never passed
suite reports a different count / a skip; the change is visible

entries.name: Swallowed exception
entries.definition: A try/except added "for robustness" deletes the failure signal.
detection_signal: Grep for except blocks whose body is only pass, continue, ..., or a log call with no counter increment.
Grep for except Exception broadly — every one is a candidate.
Compare the number of input items against the number of items actually examined, and assert equality.
entries.gate_mapping: Never discard. Either re-raise, or record a counted failure.

required_evidence.expected: the run reports it and exits non-zero
exits non-zero with "nothing was examined"; never 0 ok + exit 0

entries.name: Sentinel value on failure
entries.definition: A function returns 0.0 / "" / [] when it fails, so a crash becomes indistinguishable from a bad result.
detection_signal: Enumerate every sentinel it can return, and every legitimate value it can return.
If the two sets intersect, you have this bug.
Grep for except blocks containing return — each is a candidate.
entries.gate_mapping: Raise. Let the failure be a failure.

required_evidence.expected: raises ValueError, run aborts; no 0.0 is ever produced
raises; never reports a metric for zero records

entries.name: Neutral marker not counted
entries.definition: "Expected but absent" is reported as a neutral note, so it never increments the failure counter — and the gate prints PASS.
detection_signal: Count the checker's output states and ask, for each, whether it can produce a non-zero exit.
Then: declare what should be present. A checker that only verifies what it can find will always pass. Add an expectation list, and treat unmet expectations as failures.

required_evidence.control: Remove one required item from the source
required_evidence.expected: exits non-zero, reporting that item by name
exits non-zero; never ✅ 0 🔴 0
exits 0 — proving the check now discriminates

entries.name: Undeclared means unchecked
entries.definition: The validator checks exactly what the registry declares, so anything the registry forgot to declare is never checked — and never missed.
detection_signal: Reverse coverage. Enumerate what exists (list the published artifacts, the deployed services, the rows in the source of truth) and diff it against what is declared. Any existence not in the registry is unchecked.
Who owns registry completeness? If the answer is "whoever remembers", coverage will decay. If the answer is "an assertion in the gate", it will not.
entries.gate_mapping: Add a reverse-coverage assertion: compare the declared set against the discovered set, and treat the difference as failure in both directions.

required_evidence.control: Create a new artifact without declaring it
required_evidence.expected: gate exits non-zero, naming it as undeclared

required_evidence.control: Delete a declared item from reality
required_evidence.expected: gate exits non-zero, naming it as stale
gate exits 0

entries.name: Empty value is silent
entries.definition: A required field is empty, and nothing anywhere breaks — the page loads, the API responds, the reference resolves.
detection_signal: Enumerate the fields that a retrieval system would need in order to match this record against a query — then check whether each is populated and whether anything asserts it.
Anything with populated=no, asserted=no is this bug.
entries.gate_mapping: Split "required" into two explicit classes, and assert the second one.

required_evidence.expected: the publish path exits non-zero, naming the field
the record publishes silently — proving the assertion was doing the work

entries.name: Loading artifact as evidence of use
entries.definition: A file written at startup proves loaded. It is being read as proof of used.
detection_signal: For every metric you report, write down the claim and then ask: could this evidence be true while the claim is false?
If the rightmost column is non-empty, you are reading a proxy. Then find the event-level source: a log line with a stable, greppable shape that is emitted at the moment of the behaviour.

For the package case: match invocation events (tool '<name>' / id=<key>), not existence. Distinguish the sites that merely list the items (a roster printed in every request) from the sites that fire them — see SF-009.
entries.gate_mapping: Replace lifecycle evidence with event evidence, and state the evidence class in the report.

required_evidence.control: Install an item and never invoke it
required_evidence.expected: usage metric stays flat (correctly not counted)
usage metric increments by exactly 1

entries.name: Exposure counted as usage
entries.definition: Content is present in every request, so a search for it returns a large number — which is read as usage.
detection_signal: Inspect one instance of a hit, not the aggregate. Read the surrounding text and identify which site produced it.
Classify the sites into listing (the item is named because it is available) and firing (the item is named because it was chosen).
Count only the firing sites. A pattern that marks the firing site (a tool-call marker, an event id, a distinct log template) is the only usable counter.
entries.gate_mapping: Count events at the firing site only, and make the exclusion explicit in the query.

required_evidence.control: Add a request that does not invoke the item
required_evidence.expected: usage count unchanged (exposure rises, usage does not)
usage count +1
both counts converge — proving the gap was the inflation

entries.name: Local green is not remote green
entries.definition: Every local gate passes; the published artifact is still inconsistent, because the published artifact is a different object.
detection_signal: Is there a check that reads the live state? (Not "is there a check for the local source of it".)
Does it compare against a declared expectation, or only print what it finds?
Does it check the fields the platform rewrites — type, visibility, ordering, derived fields?
entries.gate_mapping: One read-back check per published channel, comparing live state against a declared expectation.

required_evidence.control: Change an expectation in the registry so it no longer matches live
required_evidence.expected: the check exits non-zero, naming the field

required_evidence.control: Point it at a deliberately wrong record id
required_evidence.expected: exits non-zero (not a silent no-op — see SF-001)

entries.name: The always-green oracle
entries.definition: An exemption clause fires on any match, so the check passes unconditionally — including on the exact input it exists to catch.
detection_signal: Countersign test. Feed the oracle the exact input it was built to reject. If it stays green, stop here — it does not discriminate.
Bound audit. For each exemption clause, ask: is there a lower bound? an upper bound? a maximum share? An exemption with only a lower bound ("if it matches at all, skip") is unbounded above.
Self-test in CI. Keep the pathological input as a fixture. A rule without a failing fixture is untested.
entries.gate_mapping: Make the criterion proportional and bounded, and ship the counter-example as a test.

required_evidence.expected: FAIL, reporting run length and ratio
PASS, with a near-zero ratio

required_evidence.control: Feed a text with one legitimate 20-char quote
required_evidence.expected: PASS — proves the exemption still works as intended

entries.name: Misattributed failure
entries.definition: The check fails — and blames the wrong cause, so the real defect is never fixed.
detection_signal: Take the reported cause and verify it independently. If the named cause is not actually broken, the attribution is wrong — and the real cause is still unknown.
Audit every string comparison for substring/prefix semantics where exact semantics are intended. Prefer token equality, parsed values, or anchored patterns (\b boundaries, ^...$).
Check for early return. Grep the detector for break / return inside the finding loop — each one truncates the report.
Look for a second, quieter signal. Misattribution usually means two conditions are present and only one is reported.
entries.gate_mapping: Make the comparison as strong as the claim, and report all findings rather than the first.

required_evidence.expected: reported as an exact match
reported separately as a collision, not as a field usage
both reported, not just the first

entries.name: Stale copy contaminates the check
entries.definition: A pre-change backup is written inside the directory being checked, so the check reads an old copy as fresh input.
detection_signal: Are any findings in paths that are not source? Group the report by path pattern. A cluster in .bak, _backup, ~, .orig, .tmp or a timestamped directory is this bug.
Does the count change between a clean checkout and the working tree? If yes, the difference is environmental.
Is the check's file selection explicit? If it globs a tree rather than an allow-list, it selects whatever happens to be there.

required_evidence.control: Place a .bak file with a known violation inside the tree
required_evidence.expected: gate does not report it

required_evidence.control: Place the same violation in a tracked source file
required_evidence.expected: gate does report it

required_evidence.control: Run on a clean checkout then on the working tree
required_evidence.expected: identical counts

entries.name: Zombie process looks alive
entries.definition: A hung process reports no error, holds no CPU and never exits — so every liveness signal says it is fine.
detection_signal: When did it last make progress? Not "is it alive" — "when was the last output, the last heartbeat, the last state change?"
Is there a deadline? If any job can run forever without complaint, it has no failure mode.
Are child processes reaped? Compare the expected process count against the observed count. A number that only grows is a leak.
entries.gate_mapping: Add positive progress signals, timeouts and reaping — and make the absence of progress a failure.

required_evidence.control: Make the worker hang on purpose
required_evidence.expected: watchdog kills it and reports stalled, with the silence duration

required_evidence.control: Run the worker 5 times in sequence
required_evidence.expected: resident process count returns to baseline — no accumulation
completes normally, no false stall

entries.name: Stale reference: citations rot when the cited state moves
entries.status: candidate v1.1（外审侧审阅通过带三条修改，v1.1 已按意见修订；待外审终审后转 accepted）
entries.definition: A document cites an external object's state (issue open/closed, version, link alive) but carries no re-check mechanism, so the citation silently inverts its meaning when the cited state changes.
detection_signal: Does the sentence assert a state, or a fact? States use verbs like is open / is live / is current / has been submitted. Those need a check date or no assertion.
Would the sentence still be true if the cited object changed yesterday? If the document cannot answer that, it is asserting state without liability control.
Does the citation carry (a) status-at-citation, (b) a re-check cadence matched to the volatility tier (see below), (c) a fallback wording if the state flipped? Missing any one = this bug.

Was the enumeration pulled from the source at writing time, or from memory? Memory-written enumerations are suspect by default. The pull must be complete (list the whole set, not spot-check members) — instance #3 failed precisely because a spot-check of #2/#4 was presented as the full list.

required_evidence.control: Cite a closed issue as "open question" (variant of instance #1)
required_evidence.expected: linter flags the mismatch

required_evidence.control: Cite the same issue with closure date included (fix style)
required_evidence.expected: linter passes; sentence stays true after closure
self-check question 4 triggers; enumeration re-pulled before citing
